units: <cite ref="Mishnah Peah 2:3">Peah II, 3</cite>. Y. ib. 16ᵈ <he>ג׳ מחובר</he> a hedge, v. <cite ref="H00107"><he>חָבַר</he></cite>.
B. Kam. 23ᵃ [read:] ונפל הג׳ (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l.) and the partition wall fell in; a. v. fr.—Trnsf. guard against trespassing the law, restraint, preventive measure (v. גְּזֵרָה).

<cite ref="Tosefta Shevi'it 3:13">Tosef. Shebi. III, 13</cite> <he>לא גזרו אלא ג׳ שיכול לעמוד</he> they (the scholars) erect only such a fence as can stand, i.e. enact only practicable measures (v. <cite ref="C00573"><he>גָּזַר</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 21a:24">Snh. 21ᵃ</cite> <he>ג׳ גדול גָּדְרָה וכ׳</he> Tamar erected a great guard at the time (became a warning to girls).
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 26:2">Lev. R. s. 26</cite> the serpent <he>פרץ גִּדְרוֹ של עולם</he> made a breach in the fence of the world (opened the way to lawlessness).
Lev. R. s. 24, a. fr. ג׳ ערוה guard against immorality, chastity, v. גָּדַר; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 1:4:4">Y. Pes. I, 27ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>ויש ג׳ לג׳</he> can a preventive rabbinical law (<cite ref="C00581"><he>גְּזֵרָה</he></cite>) be enacted as a guard for another preventive law?—Pl. <he>גְּדֵרוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 24:6">Lev. R. s. 24</cite>; a. e., v. <cite ref="C00213"><he>גָּדֵיר</he></cite>.
